definition: The practice of tracking and managing changes to prompts over time, similar to how source code is version-controlled.
details: Prompt versioning allows teams to test, roll back, and audit changes to prompts used in production, treating prompts as a first-class engineering artifact rather than an informal, untracked text string.

explainer.lead: Tracking and managing changes to prompts over time, much like version-controlling source code. It lets teams test, roll back, and audit production prompts as first-class engineering artifacts.

tiers.eli5: It is like keeping drafts of a message with dates, so you can see what changed and go back to an earlier version if needed.
tiers.practitioner: Teams store prompt revisions so changes can be compared, rolled back, and audited in production. A pitfall is treating prompts as informal untracked strings, making regressions hard to trace.
tiers.paperLevel: Practice rather than a formal method: prompts are treated as versioned artifacts with tracked changes; no formal definition or formula is specified.

explainer.example: A team ships prompt v3, sees worse results, and rolls back to v2 because both versions were tracked.
